items.title: Shanto: 'Very important for the whole batting unit to perform'
items.summary: The Bangladesh captain said their bowling attack can "compete" if the batters post a big total in the first innings

items.title: On-song South Africa host Bangladesh with an eye on another WTC final
items.summary: Hamza and Paterson return to South Africa's XI in what is Johannesburg's first Test since March 2023

items.title: Shanto urges batting unit to step up against Proteas amid praise for pace attack
items.summary: Shanto made it clear during his pre-match press conference on Saturday that the entire batting unit needs to step up if the visitors are to challenge hosts South Africa in the opening Test of the two-match series, which begins on Sunday at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg.

items.title: Mosaddek ends eight-year wait for first-class ton
items.summary: Mosaddek's previous first-class hundred came in 2018, when he scored 104 for Central Zone against North Zone in a Bangladesh Cricket League (BCL) match.

items.title: Proteas opt for four-pronged pace attack against Tigers in Johannesburg Test
items.summary: Alongside their pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada and Dane Paterson, the Proteas have included pace-bowling all-rounders Wiaan Mulder and Marco Jansen, indicating their intention to exploit the conditions at the Wanderers. Harmer is the lone specialist spinner in the attack.

items.title: Can Tigers repeat Darwin against Bavuma's formidable Proteas?
items.summary: With 13 victories in his first 15 Tests in charge, Bavuma has matched a record achieved only by Australia's Lindsay Hassett at the same stage of his captaincy. Both registered 13 wins, one draw and one defeat in their first 15 matches, making the South African the most successful Test captain at this stage of his tenure alongside the Australian.

items.title: Tigresses bounce back with Zimbabwe victory; Nahida ruled out
items.summary: Bangladesh will not bring in a replacement for Nahida, as they travelled to the UAE with an extra member, although tournament regulations require teams to have 14 players.

items.title: Rabada 'chuffed at engagement from fans' after series win against Australia
items.summary: Series against Bangladesh begins on Sunday, and Rabada hopes "some exciting cricket" shows "how healthy cricket is" in SA

items.title: Rizwanullah, openers set up big win as Pakistan make U-19 Asia Cup final
items.summary: Rizwanullah's five-for restricted Bangladesh to 138 following which Usman Khan and Hayam Khan mowed down the target with ease

items.title: Shanto: Bangladesh failed to make use of home conditions

items.title: Dale Benkenstein appointed Bangladesh's batting specialist ahead of SA tour
items.summary: Bangladesh are scheduled to tour South Africa in November and December 2026 to play two Tests, three ODIs and three T20Is
